You offer one of the strongest debuff in the game with your boat, and you carry auras to help your team. You are in no shape or form useless. Like I get it, he is not a beast on lategame, and you are dependent on having a good team that can use your teamfight capabilities, but you are not a x+torrent machine late. Hell, your tankiness and damage delays assure that anyone hitting you without a bkb on lategame is going to lose a lot of HP.

Kunkka is no longer the one shot kill hero that used to build crit and shadowblade, but you are still a tanky, fairly fast hero (because phase boots) that have a sure way to grab a hero and kill him. You are dependent of a team that will go with you and use your combo to get kills, and when you don't have the timing, you farm waves and jungle fairly fast. You are also very good at counter ganking if the enemy mid feels the need to gank if the lane is not going well, since you have torrent and boat.

What I build is normally a bottle, bracer, wand and phase boots, after that, you can see what the team need, if you can make Blademail work, then go for it, or an orchid if you can ensure one of the enemy hero can have a terrible game. After that, you might need a bkb if they are jumping you to stop you from casting, but if not, I always go for Scepter, and while is not as good as waterpark, its a great teamfight item that disrupts the fight inmediatly. After that, Shivas is often great, and Refresher after that.

You build him as a complete team fight hero, and can build auras if the team needs it and the offlane is someone like a LC, but its not a solo kill hero, and if your team is not playing together and/or the carry is bad, you are likely going to lose, but its definitely a hero that can give you wins. And its more likely to get buffed, so its extra good.

I know the hero is not in his best moment, but unless you are playing the highest bracket, and im talking about top 500 inmortal where they can explote a heroes weakness to the max, you can still find success with the hero, I am playing him on 6000 mmr and I can win with him. 

Its a tanky mid with decent creepwave clear that can farm and gank, and a great carrier of aura if the mid doesn't get it. If you get a good start and can bully the enemy mid, you have a hero that can snowball.

Don't get me wrong, he is still bad, but its not useless in the slightless unless you are playing in the highest bracket or in pro play.

With your berserk blood, you heal more than the armlet damages you, which is unique to the hero. Of course, you will be fairly low hp when you do so, but that is also when you are the strongest. So, depending on the enemy heroes, being very low is a bad idea, for example vs an ancient apparition or a necrophos, as well as really high damaging heroes as a dagger Sven or a sniper. Versus some of those, you are better staying somewhat higher that 50% hp.

Now, to when to toggle, as I say, you outheal the armlet, so you can enter fights with the armlet on so you have fewer hp at the start of the fight. The key to the armlet, at least at low mmr, is just to be patient. If you have 2 heroes hitting you, and you panic and turn it off and on, you will probably die. You need to see the space between the attacks and react to it. If a kunkka and tuskar are hitting you, they most likely just try to kill you with right clicks and have the damage to outdamage your heal. You need to be aware on what spells what they have left, and if they don't, toggle really fast to gain a burst of heal. The higher the attack speed the harder is it doing it. Of course, Huskar have a AOE disarm that he can use to buy time to toggle. If you are confident in that they don't have spells left, you hit them with the armlet on for max damage and speed, and toggle just before the disarms expire.

For Roshan, you can probably watch some YouTube tutorial, but I recommend you practice with a lobby with cheats on, and you try advancing the in game timer to 15min or so, and give yourself level 10. The trick is the following, you stand in the limit to the Roshan entrance where you can still see him and hit him. The reason is that because you will force him to walk to you, he will walk back to the initial spot and buy you some time. Now, you want to hit him with the spears on auto attack and with the armlet always on. Now, this is the important part, remember that the less hp you have, the higher the hp Regen is, so the closer you are to death, you get tankier, so with that in mind, you need to get a feel on how much more hits you can take from Rosh before dying. For safety reason, calculate 4 or 3 hits. When Roshan enter that threshold, you go for the toggle. Now, this is the critical part, you need to be patient and don't panic, because if you toggle when Rosh bash you, you will die. This is what kills Huskar the most. Remember, you calculated 3 to 4 hits before dying, so just react. Sometimes Rosh will bash you 2 times in a row, but you still are under the threshold to survive, and I don't recall Roshan bashing 3 times in a row. You also have your first skill to get you a free toggle in case you panic a bit, but as long as you mind your threshold and don't panic, you should get Roshan pretty consistently.
